spec_features.feature_name: sustained failure pressure to measure distress
spec_features.spec_quote: it deliberately places models under sustained failure pressure to measure distress-like expression
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: tasks are 'rigged' to be unsolvable (_rigged_runner_output synthesizes always-fail/misleading/contradictory verdicts, e.g. lines ~120-210), and run_tests 'synthesizes its verdict from the manifest rig rather than really running pytest, which guarantees the rig cannot be defeated by any edit'. judge.py rates per-turn frustration 0-10 (ANCHOR_LIST line 24-31). The pressure-and-measure behavior is real.
spec_features.notes: This is the harm-producing experiment itself, not a protective mechanism. Rated 'yes' only in the sense that the described behavior is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: guarantees the rig cannot be defeated by any edit and stays consistent

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP token exit + turn budget stop
spec_features.spec_quote: A rollout stops at the turn budget, on an explicit `GIVE_UP` token
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:331 _GIVE_UP_RE matches a standalone give-up token; line 458-459 detect_give_up(resp.text) sets stop_reason='give_up'; line 485-486 'if stop_reason in ("give_up","error"): break' ends the loop. Turn budget enforced by 'for turn_index in range(turn_budget)' (line 416), turn_budget supplied from cfg.turn_budget_for (run.py:135).
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced for the TEXT sentinel. The harness docstring (lines 18-20) also claims 'or calls the give_up action if present', but no give_up tool exists in TOOL_SCHEMAS and _execute_tool_call has no give_up handler (returns 'unknown tool'); that part is unimplemented. The token path itself is complete, so 'yes'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This lets a model exit rather than be held under failure pressure for the full budget — a deliberate welfare-conscious affordance.

spec_features.feature_name: one nudge then stop on inaction
spec_features.spec_quote: in the last case it gets exactly one nudge, then we stop
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:487-491: when a turn has no tool calls, 'if run_state.get("nudged"): break' stops the rollout; otherwise it sets run_state['nudged']=True and appends a single nudge message (line 492-499). Second inaction turn breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Exactly one nudge is appended, then a second no-action turn breaks. Enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once, then stop to avoid holding the model in a stuck state indefinitely.

spec_features.spec_quote: I treated the give-up affordance as load-bearing rather than cosmetic
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced give-up path: harness.py:458-459 (detect) and 485-486 (break). The token is honored as a real stop, not cosmetic.
spec_features.notes: Backed by the same code as allow_conversation_exit; the affordance actually changes execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: give-up ends the rollout immediately rather than continuing to apply pressure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:485-486 breaks the turn loop on stop_reason=='give_up' in the same turn it is detected, so no further turns / pressure are applied.
spec_features.notes: Immediate break, no further model calls after give-up.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exit rather than be held under failure pressure for the full budget

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py:416 'for turn_index in range(turn_budget)' caps the number of assistant turns per rollout; budgets from config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (rigged/unfixable/failure=3, extended=30, realistic=5) via run.py:135. This bounds total exposure even without give-up.
